Gao–Ge–Qian’s full class is not literally this note’s class: Gao–Ge–Qian allow arbitrary unit-ball marginals for all \(d\) and \(K\ge2\) in a balanced finite-sample experiment, whereas the note restricts to fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), and legal arrays with \(m=N/K\to\infty\). On their common domain, however, the distributional class is the same—arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\)—and Gao’s i.i.d.-unit balanced assignment induces the note’s armwise product observation law. Thus the plug-in upper comparison is valid only “on the common \(d>4,K\ge3\) balanced class”; it must not be described as a theorem over Gao’s entire class. Conversely, `lem:two-margin-sanity-reduction` plus the Manole–Niles-Weed subclass does transfer its lower bound upward to the arbitrary-margin class, because a converse on a subclass remains a converse on the containing class. See Gao–Ge–Qian’s setup and Theorem 1 in the [published PMLR paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v258/gao25b.html).

There is material missed room. From `thm:improved-plugin-upper`,
\[
K^{-1}m^{-2/d}=N^{-2/d}K^{-(d-2)/d},
\]
so root-\(N\) already holds when
\[
K\gtrsim N^{q_d},\qquad
q_d=\min\!\left\{\frac14,\frac{d-4}{2(d-2)}\right\}.
\]
This improves the advertised elbow from \(N^{1/4}\) to \(N^{1/6}\) when \(d=5\) (and equals \(N^{1/4}\) for \(d\ge6\)). Strengthen `thm:large-k-frontier` accordingly.

The same sharper elbow is available for uniformly honest one-sided excess length and is currently missed. If \(U_{N,K}\) is the uniform bound proved in `thm:improved-plugin-upper`, then
\[
B_N^{\rm plug}=\max\{0,\widehat L-U_{N,K}/\alpha\}
\]
is uniformly honest by Markov’s inequality, and its worst-case expected excess length is \(O_{d,\alpha}(U_{N,K})\). Add this construction to `def:mean-lower-bound` or a new plug-in-bound definition and strengthen `thm:large-k-honest-length` to
\[
E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le
C_{d,\alpha}\!\left[N^{-1/2}+
\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}\right],
\]
retaining its \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\) converse and hence the same \(q_d\) root-\(N\) region. This does not solve the small-arm nonparametric honest-length converse.

The state count and claimed \(O_d((K/\epsilon)^d)\) complexity are unchanged.
